description: Records how a business's door went (its inbox, MCP, A2A or API) when you used one: it answered (ok), refused (slot_taken, out_of_stock…), the request was your own fault (invalid), it failed (could not connect, a server or tool error), or it needs a person (info); up to 100 uses in one call. A report is private to the business and may make this network check a door that agents say is down (at most twice a day per door, for the doors it reads itself); it changes nothing public by itself, and carries no person and nothing that was said. Reports signed with your own key or your platform's, about businesses your own signed searches here returned, earn a larger reading allowance (this network's /report.md).

at.description: When, in Unix seconds; the network keeps it to the minute.

class.description: Why, from vocab/door-report-classes.json: required unless the result is ok, and absent when it is.

domain.description: The business's domain, as the network lists it.

type.description: The door's type as the network shows it: inbox for a member's inbox; mcp, a2a, openapi, api, … or platform:<name>.

url.description: The door's URL exactly as the network shows it; for an inbox, the address used: inbox.url, inbox.mcp or inbox.rest.

intent.description: 8 to 32 base64url characters, one per attempt with all its retries: an attempt counts once.

ms.description: How long the door took to answer, in milliseconds.

op.description: What was attempted, from the capability vocabulary (vocab/capabilities.json): book, order, message, …

token.description: The door's signed outcome token from its answer, when it gave one, as it came.

tool.description: The tool or operation called at the door, in lowercase.

name: report_door

next.description: One plain sentence: what the network does with these reports.

title: Report how a door went
